findings.title: Integer coercion can silently change exact real values
findings.description: `as_integer` converts every non-`Integral` `Real` to `float` before converting it to `int`. An exact integral `Fraction` above the float precision limit can therefore be accepted as a *different* integer—for example, `Fraction(2**53 + 1, 1)` becomes `2**53`. Since parameter binding uses this coercion, a supplied value can be bound and canonicalized incorrectly. Preserve the value’s exactness when checking integral `Real` inputs, or reject values that cannot be converted without loss.

findings.title: Invalid timestamp meanings raise `AttributeError` instead of `InvalidSignalError`
findings.description: `Timestamp` does not validate that `meaning` is a `TimeMeaning` (`timestamps.py:57` only checks the nanosecond range). If a timestamp is constructed with an invalid meaning, this branch tries to read `self.time.meaning.value` while building the error and raises `AttributeError`. Validate the meaning’s type before accessing `.value`, so malformed input is reported through the signal validation error contract.
